qc.label_under_test: intensifier 'much'/'still' (Russian еще) right before a comparative or quantity

neighbours.label: 'much' (or viel, beaucoup, гораздо; Russian еще, так) used as a degree booster right before an adjective or comparative; not 'much' as a quantity (how much, much of, too much), and weak for very/far/quite
fire: The new train is much faster than the old one.
After the rain stopped, the air felt much cooler on the porch.
She was much happier once she moved closer to her sister.
This recipe turned out much better than the one we tried last week.
Honestly, the second book is much longer and much darker than the first.
Der neue Laptop ist viel schneller als mein alter.
Im Winter ist es hier viel kälter als an der Küste.
Ce nouveau modèle est beaucoup plus léger que le précédent.
quiet: The new train carries much of the freight from the old line.
After the rain stopped, there was too much water on the porch.
She wondered how much her sister had paid for the move.
This recipe uses much butter and not a lot of sugar.
Honestly, the second book did not interest me that much at all.
Der neue Laptop kostet viel Geld, also spare ich noch.
Im Winter fällt hier viel Schnee an der Küste.
Ce nouveau modèle consomme beaucoup d'essence chaque mois.

predictions: Expect most English much+adjective sentences to fire; German/French may be weaker; quantity 'much' near misses quiet.
